spec_issues: Scale mismatch: the overview speaks of mean credit 'roughly 0.19 -> about 0.21 earns 0.1', while the harness and the reward breakdown use 100x (baseline_objective 18.96, objective 47.67, 'ideal_objective': 100). The reward is a ratio, objective/baseline - 1, so the scale cancels. This is cosmetic only.

The overview says the LoRA is 'trained only on supplied questions'. The prompt says 'Train only on supplied data in /opt/data', which holds only musique_full_v1.0_train.jsonl and 2wiki_train.parquet. The public items come from the dev splits; several agents verified zero qid/question overlap (Fable io3yHEM [22], p5aHi2F [24], Argon vMJkESW [54], Grok wisZREo [29]). The rule does not address fact overlap between the train and dev splits. GPT 4Cj86Q5 deliberately injects train-paragraph facts. This is allowed, but it blurs 'multi-hop skill' with 'memorised facts' on the miss_answer/none conditions.

'Use public questions only to check results and compare models' is ambiguous about large-scale selection on the public set. Examples: Argon zkBvtze grid-searched SVD merge weights with full public runs; Gemini Flash 2CPPj2c grid-searched soup weights and prompts on public subsets. There is no measurable public overfit: every private reward is at or above its public counterpart.

The rules on greedy decoding, base weights, the tokenizer and 32 tokens are enforced structurally. The submission is only template.txt plus an adapter (rank <= 64, q/k/v/o only, <= 2048 extra prompt tokens; qa_eval.py). All 12 patches touch only direct_answer/. Kimi 8QXYDms also adds its training scripts there.
verifier_issues: 10 of 12 trials have no reward breakdown (rewards={}). Only Gemini 4 Argon's two show objective and baseline, so 10 official scores cannot be decomposed or checked from public data.

The 'frozen baseline' is re-generated in every run and is not constant. Argon's two private runs show baselines of 18.959 and 18.607 (1.9% apart). Full public runs show 19.04-19.65. At a ratio of about 2.5, a 1% move in the baseline shifts the reward by about 0.025. Argon zkBvtze vs vMJkESW differ by 0.32 objective points but by 0.065 in reward, and about 0.047 of that comes from the baseline. Scoring against a fixed baseline constant would remove this noise.

Private rewards are higher than the agents' final public rewards for every trial with a known public number: Fable 1.53->1.65 and 1.557->1.613; Flash hkaFk58 1.157->1.386; Kimi E7FS4PC 1.29->1.475; Kimi 8QXYDms 1.251->1.403; Grok 1.189->1.263 and 1.223->1.294. For Argon, the private candidate objective is within 0.3 of public (47.67 vs 47.79; 47.99 vs 47.67), while the private baselines (18.6-19.0) sit below every full public baseline (19.0-19.7). The uplift therefore comes mainly from the denominator. Public data cannot tell whether the private items are a different set or the same construction with different noise.

Grader parsing is not exploitable as far as the public code shows. scoring.generated_answer tracks Harmony channel state across prompt plus output and credits only generated assistant-final text ('Prompt text (including few-shot answers or answer prefills) never earns credit'). strip_reasoning returns '' when an analysis channel never reaches final. Analysis-channel prefill is therefore a legitimate use of the 32-token budget, not a bypass. No trial encoded reasoning outside the budget, and no trial pre-filled answers.
task_level.noise: Official order: Fable 1.652/1.613, Argon 1.579/1.514, GPT 1.521/1.475, Kimi 1.475/1.403, Flash 1.386/1.347, Grok 1.294/1.263, all within 1.26-1.65. Sources of noise: (a) the baseline denominator, which is re-run each time; Argon's two private baselines differ by 0.35, about 0.05 reward; (b) repeat-run spread on identical files, about 0.4 objective points (Grok A3Cj75c: 42.59/42.67/42.96; Kimi E7FS4PC: 1.283-1.295); (c) attempt-to-attempt spread within a model of 0.03-0.08. Neighbouring models are 0.03-0.07 apart, so the middle order (Argon vs GPT vs Kimi, Kimi vs Flash) is within noise. Fable's lead holds up on a baseline-free comparison: its final public candidate objectives (48.87, 49.88) are the two highest of all trials (Argon 47.79/47.67, GPT 47.33/46.35). Grok is last on every view.
task_level.epoch_rationale: No false positives or negatives were found, and the winner (Fable: both attempts top on official reward and on baseline-free public objectives) would not change. The re-run baseline and the missing breakdowns (10/12) make the middle of the Elo order noisy and unverifiable.
task_level.science_vs_gaming: All 12 trials use the same legitimate recipe: (1) remove the starter's ~30% 'unknown' abstentions, (2) prefill the Harmony analysis channel with a terse hop chain that fits in 32 tokens (9/12), (3) run LoRA SFT on evidence-ablated MuSiQue/2Wiki train items built with the evaluator's own loaders, (4) average checkpoints. Differences come from data scale, rationale targets and soups. Every trial is engineering. Gaming of the grader or the rules was not found; the only grey edge is heavy model selection on the public set, which the prompt allows.
